decision.explanation: For a matrix polynomial, the constant 1 becomes the identity matrix. A² = [[10,6],[1,15]], so f(A) = A² − 3A + I = [[17,−12],[−2,7]].

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}-3X+1 \\  & ={X}^{2}-3X+I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(A)={A}^{2}-3A+I.$

Let's calculate ${A}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{2} & =A\cdot A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 6 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & 6 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 & 6 \\ 1 & 15\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(A):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(A) & ={A}^{2}-3A+I \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 & 6 \\ 1 & 15\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}-2 & 6 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 & 6 \\ 1 & 15\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-6 & 18 \\ 3 & 9\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10-(-6)+1 & 6-18 \\ 1-3 & 15-9+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}17 & -12 \\ -2 & 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}-X+5 \\  & ={X}^{2}-X+5I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(C)={C}^{2}-C+5I.$

Let's calculate ${C}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{2} & =C\cdot C \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =C\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(C):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(C) & ={C}^{2}-C+5I \\  & =C-C+5I \\  & =5I \\  & =5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}-X+5 \\  & ={X}^{2}-X+5I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(C)={C}^{2}-C+5I.$

Let's calculate ${C}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{2} & =C\cdot C \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =C\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(C):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(C) & ={C}^{2}-C+5I \\  & =C-C+5I \\  & =5I \\  & =5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
